images.title: Less, right, more
images.purpose: Angles can be sorted by comparing them with a right angle: smaller than a right angle is acute, bigger than a right angle but smaller than a straight angle is obtuse.
images.composition: Three angles in a row, all sharing the same horizontal base direction, wide gaps between them.
images.exact_structure: Left: an acute angle of exactly 45 degrees in teal #0072B2. Middle: a right angle of exactly 90 degrees in grey #6B7280 with a small square corner mark. Right: an obtuse angle of exactly 135 degrees in amber #E69F00. All arms exactly the same length, each with a small arc. Exactly 3 angles.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any of the following: degree numbers on the angles
images.takeaway: Compare each angle with a right angle to name it.
images.description: Three angles in a row: a narrow teal acute angle, a grey right angle with a square mark, and a wide amber obtuse angle.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at the right angle and say whether each other angle is smaller or bigger.

image_decisions.why: Sorting angles against a right angle is a picture idea; three angles in a row carry it.
